programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Czechia v Mexico (Kick-off 2.00am). Coverage of the Group A match at Mexico City Stadium. The Mexicans were undefeated in the six matches they played here when hosting the 1970 and 1986 World Cups, and have continued in the same vein this time around, with a victory over South Africa here, before another win in Zapopan against South Korea ensured they were the first team to secure a place in the round of 32 and top spot in the group. In contrast, the Czechs have disappointed so far, collecting just one point against the South Africans, but a win would almost certainly send them through, either in second or as one of the best third-place teams

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Ecuador v Germany (Kick-off 9.00pm). Kelly Cates presents coverage of the Group E match at New York/New Jersey Stadium in the USA. Germany have already won the group, thanks to an injury-time winner against Ivory Coast that made it two wins from two for them, while Ecuador realistically need a win to qualify for the knockout stages. This will be the third overall meeting between these nations, and their second as part of a group stage at a World Cup after previously being drawn alongside each other at the 2006 tournament in Germany. Die Mannschaft were 3-0 winners on that occasion courtesy of a brace from Miroslav Klose and one from Lukas Podolski, which was also the final clash of the group stage, and resulted in both teams progressing to the knockout stage with Germany topping the table and La Tricolor finishing second. With analysis from Daniel Sturridge, Joe Hart and Lucas Leiva

programme.title: MOTD Live: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Japan v Sweden (Kick-off 12.00am). Coverage of the Group F match at Dallas Stadium in the USA. This is one of the tightest groups of the tournament, with Japan undefeated after a draw against the Netherlands and a win against Tunisia, while Sweden know that a point should be enough to see them progress to the last 31, despite a heavy defeat to the Dutch last time out. At their seven previous appearances at the finals Japan have progressed to the knockout stage four times, including at the two previous tournaments in 2018 and 2022. While they finished strongly four years ago with a 2-1 win over Spain that saw them top the table, a 1-0 loss to Poland in Volgograd eight years ago meant they had to rely on Senegal also losing in their clash against Colombia and also becoming the first nation to benefit from the fair play rule to break a tied record with the unfortunate Africans. In another memorable first, Japan became the first Asian country to compete at an international tournament when they appeared in the football competition at the 1936 Olympics in Berlin, and on that occasion, they claimed a 3-2 victory over Sweden, which was seen as a massive shock at the time

Starring an Oscar-winning Will Smith alongside Aunjanue Ellis, Jon Bernthal, Saniyya Sidney and Demi Singleton

With no World Cup experience to speak of, Curaçao will rely heavily on their Dutch coach Dick Advocaat, who has enjoyed an extensive career in both club and international football, the latter including three spells in charge of the Netherlands, in addition to roles at the helm of the UAE, South Korea, Belgium, Russia, Serbia and Iraq. Ivory Coast are managed by Emerse Faé, who earned 41 caps as a player after initially having represented his native France at under-21 level, and was appointed to this job midway through the 2023 Africa Cup of Nations after stepping up from his role in charge of the under-23s, upon which he led them to win the tournament

This is the first-ever competitive match between these nations, with all three previous encounters in 1978, 1994 and 2009 being friendly matches. programme.title: The Accused: Beyond Reasonable Doubt?
programme.desc: Following individuals fighting convictions that they believe to be a miscarriage of justice. At a time when the British justice system is under scrutiny, this documentary explores how difficult it is to overturn a guilty verdict, revealing the emotional toll, legal hurdles and determination required to prove innocence. Beginning with a look at the case of Jason Moore, who was found guilty of murder in 2005 after a man was killed during a street fight he was involved in. Jason's family and close friends have fought tirelessly to campaign for his innocence and even enrolled an unlikely supporter: the victim's brother. When new evidence emerges, casting doubt on the eye-witness account, is it the key to freeing Jason?

programme.title: Murdered: The Baby on the Beach
programme.desc: How the discovery of a five-day-old boy's body on a lonely Co Kerry beach in April 1984 set in train a chain of events that would bring shame on the-then conservatively minded Irish state and the Gardai. An innocent woman was accused of murdering her child, leading to a tribunal now recognised as a witch hunt

programme.title: Murdered: The Baby on the Beach
programme.desc: The prosecutor makes a crucial decision to drop the charges against Joanne Hayes and the family. programme.title: Murdered: The Baby on the Beach

programme.title: The Accused: Beyond Reasonable Doubt?

Stacey insisted she was defending herself and her friend. But as her criminal charge reached court, the jury saw differently and found her guilty of murder. Those close to Stacey stood by her and searched for a way to prove that she acted in self-defence. Could the charity Justice for Women offer a way out? Stacey Hyde's case is one of many in which women who kill are imprisoned for murder, even though the courts may not have fully examined the circumstances that led to the event

programme.title: The M Factor: Shredding the Silence on Menopause
programme.desc: Menopause is a silent epidemic that affects the health and wellbeing of millions of women. In addition to experiencing traumatic physical symptoms, women often struggle with related emotional stresses. Despite its universality, menopause remains mired in silence and misinformation, exacerbating the broader crisis in women's health. Symptoms can derail careers, disrupt relationships and cause unnecessary physical suffering. This film confronts this neglected crisis, challenges societal and medical misunderstandings, and advocates for a revolutionary approach to women's health

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Norway v France (Kick-off 8.00pm). Joanne Cantwell presents all the action from the final match in Group I for both teams, held at Boston Stadium in the USA. This is the first meeting between the teams since 2014, when France prevailed 4-0 in a friendly. The French are likely to go into this fixture as favourites to prevail once again, but a close contest is anticipated. Should they both be available, the game could see two of the world's leading forwards go head to head in Frenchman Kylian Mbappe and Norway's Erling Haaland, and it would be little surprise if either one of them proved to be the difference-maker this evening. Both teams have already progressed to the knock-out stages after winning both of their opening games, and France will finish top of the group if they avoid defeat here

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: Cape Verde v Saudi Arabia (Kick-off 1.00am). All the action from both teams' third and final Group H match, held at Houston Stadium in the USA. Uruguay and Spain were the two favourites to qualify from this group, but even if both of these sides have failed to collect a point so far, with eight of the 12 third-placed teams qualifying for the last 32, three points here could be enough to see either one of them progress. The only time the Saudis managed to reach the knockout stage was in 1994, when the United States served as hosts, while this is the first time Cape Verde have played in the finals. Both of these sides still have a chance of progressing to the knock-out stages and a victory here may well do the job. This is the first meeting between the teams since 2014, when France prevailed 4-0 in a friendly. The French are likely to go into this fixture as favourites to prevail once again, but a close contest is anticipated. Should they both be available, the game could see two of the world's leading forwards go head to head in Frenchman Kylian Mbappe and Norway's Erling Haaland, and it would be little surprise if either one of them proved to be the difference-maker this evening. Both teams have already progressed to the knock-out stages after winning both of their opening games, and France will finish top of the group if they avoid defeat here

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 26 Live
programme.desc: New Zealand v Belgium (Kick-off 4.00am). Group G reaches a climax at BC Place Vancouver in Canada, with this first-ever meeting between the nations. It's perhaps not surprising that this is a first encounter, as the All Whites have only reached the World Cup finals on two previous occasions, the first of which was a memorable campaign back in 1982, when they lost all three matches but still managed to play a part in Scotland being eliminated at the first hurdle once again. Belgium are unlikely to have as much attention focused on them this time than in recent years, when they were often tipped for success, but that may remove some of the pressure that has weighed so heavily on their shoulders. Both of these sides need a victory here to have any chance of progressing to the knock-out stages, with the top two in the group facing each other in the other group match taking place tonight. programme.title: Rik Mayall: Magnificent B'stard
programme.desc: A documentary tribute to the influential and much-missed comedian, a man driven by punk spirit and an unrelenting commitment to pushing boundaries. When he died in 2014 at the age of 56, Rik left behind a body of ground-breaking work, from Rick the Poet and Kevin Turvey to The Young Ones, Bottom and The New Statesman - performances that redefined television comedy and helped ignite the alternative comedy revolution. The film explores his comedic journey, his creative partnership with Adrian Edmondson, his struggle with drink and the near-fatal quad-bike accident that left him fighting not only for his life but also his future. Contributors include Stephen Fry, Ben Elton, Greg Davies, Paul Jackson, John Lloyd, Nigel Planer and Adrian Edmondson

programme.title: I'm Chevy Chase and You're Not
programme.desc: Chevy Chase was a cast member on the inaugural series of Saturday Night Live and he built on that success to star in numerous Hollywood comedies and host the Academy Awards. He played hapless father Clark Griswold in the National Lampoon films and ran amok in pictures including Caddyshack, Spies Like Us, Fletch and Three Amigos. Two-time Emmy Award winner Marina Zenovich directs an authorised feature-length documentary portrait of Chase, which includes rare and intimate home movies and archive footage. Chase and his family share memories directly to camera, enriched with contributions from friends and collaborators including Dan Aykroyd, Beverly D'Angelo, Goldie Hawn, Lorne Michaels, Ryan Reynolds and Martin Short.

programme.desc: The adventurer reaches Sri Lanka, whose strategic location and tropical spices made it a target for invaders and colonisers for centuries. On his way to Bangladesh, he hitches a ride on a trawler, highlighting one of the Indian Ocean's fastest-growing industries - providing prawns for the West. But as he reveals, it comes at a price for the environment

programme.title: Indian Ocean with Simon Reeve

He also explores the illegal trade in exotic pets in the Indonesian capital of Jakarta, before heading for Australia, the final country on his epic journey. There he visits the unspoilt wilderness of the Kimberley region, meets a crocodile hunter and goes fishing with natives campaigning to stop the construction of a giant gas plant
